paper_metadata.title: Intellectual outcome from 1 to 5 years after epilepsy surgery in 81 children and adolescents: A longitudinal study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the target population, recruitment setting (tertiary center), and explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria. The sample is representative of school-aged children with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing resective surgery.

items.label: Source of target population

items.evidence_snippet: children with refractory focal epilepsy followed in the Marseille tertiary epilepsy center by the multidisciplinary team... at the La Timone and Henri Gastaut hospitals in Marseille, France.
items.reasoning: The authors specify the clinical condition and the specific healthcare setting.

items.evidence_snippet: We included 81 patients who underwent surgical treatment from 2000 to 2018.
items.reasoning: The study uses a consecutive cohort from a specialized multidisciplinary team over an 18-year period.

(c) multidisciplinary team discussion (d) intellectual skills... allowing reliable testing... We excluded patients who underwent extensive (hemispherotomy) or palliative surgery.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (seizure freedom, localization, age) are clearly defined and measured using standard clinical and surgical records. The use of Engel classification for seizure outcome is a validated standard.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Postoperative seizure control was classified using Engel's classification criteria... patients were deemed "seizure-free" if they did not have a seizure since the surgery (Engel class Ia).
items.reasoning: The primary prognostic factor (seizure freedom) is explicitly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF

items.evidence_snippet: Postoperative seizure control was classified using Engel's classification criteria.
items.reasoning: Engel's classification is the gold standard in epilepsy surgery research.

risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (intellectual change) was measured using standardized, age-appropriate Wechsler scales. The definition of 'improvement' or 'decline' (10 points) was pre-specified to exceed the standard error of measurement.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: a patient was said to be "improved" if the change between pre-and post-surgery was greater than +10 points, "decreased" if the change was greater than - 10 points.
items.reasoning: The threshold for significant intellectual change is clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Age-appropriate Wechsler Intelligence Scales (WISC IV or WAIS-III) were used... inter-correlations between the different test versions were very high.
items.reasoning: The Wechsler scales are validated, reliable instruments for IQ measurement.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All assessments reported in this study were conducted by the same neuropsychologist (V.L).
items.reasoning: A single assessor using standardized tests ensures high consistency.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the authors adjusted for several key variables (age, localization, ASM) in a multivariable model, the retrospective nature and the lack of a control group make it difficult to fully account for the 'practice effect' or natural maturation, despite the 10-point threshold.

items.reasoning: A wide range of clinical and demographic confounders were captured.
